cards.text: Paul's a prisoner in Caesarea, kept under guard in Herod's Praetorium until Felix, the governor, hears his case (Acts 23:33-35). Five days later, the high priest Ananias comes down with some elders. Friend, these men did NOT come to say hi.

cards.question: Ananias and the elders are here to present their case against Paul to the governor. Who do they bring along to do the presenting?

cards.text: Elders AND a lawyer. Friend, that's a whole legal TEAM for one prisoner.

cards.question: Paul is called in, and Tertullus opens the prosecution. But his first words aren't about Paul. They're about Felix, the man deciding the case. What does Tertullus say?

answers.text: Felix brought this nation lasting peace
Felix has kept them waiting too long
Felix should send Paul to Rome

cards.text: And he lays it on THICK: “In every way and everywhere, most excellent Felix, we acknowledge this with all gratitude.” That's the coworker who LOVES the boss's tie right before asking for Friday off.
Then Tertullus promises to keep it brief, and here come the charges. He calls Paul a pestilence, stirring up dissension among the Jews all over the world.

cards.question: Tertullus brings up the sect of the Nazarenes. What does he say Paul is in that sect?
Tertullus says Paul even tried to desecrate the temple, so they ___ him.

cards.text: Tertullus wraps it up. Examine him yourself, Felix, and you'll learn the truth about all our charges.

cards.question: When Tertullus finishes, the Jews with him back him up and say his charges are true.

cards.text: Now the governor motions for Paul to speak. Ananias brought a lawyer, and Paul brought… PAUL.

cards.question: Paul says that since Felix has been a judge over this nation for many years, Paul makes his defense ___.
Paul tells Felix he can check it: no more than twelve days ago, Paul went up to Jerusalem to ___.
Paul says his accusers found him debating in the temple and riling up a crowd.

cards.text: Paul says they can't prove any of their charges against him. But then he does confess one thing.

cards.question: Paul confesses one thing to Felix. What is it?

answers.text: He worships God according to the Way
He brought a Greek into the temple
He speaks against the Law of Moses

cards.text: The Way, which his accusers call a sect. And Paul says he believes everything laid down by the Law and written in the Prophets.

cards.question: Paul says he shares the same hope in God that his accusers cherish. It's a hope about what happens after death. What is it?

answers.text: The righteous and the wicked will rise again
Only the righteous will rise again
Their names will live on forever

cards.text: In this hope, Paul says, he always strives to keep a clear conscience before God and man.
Paul's still making his defense before Felix. He says that after several years away, he came back to Jerusalem.

cards.question: Why does Paul say he came back to Jerusalem after several years away?

answers.text: To bring alms and present offerings
To answer charges before the Sanhedrin
To confront the men who opposed him

cards.question: Paul says that when they found him in the temple, he was ceremonially clean.

cards.text: Then Paul says some Jews from the province of Asia ought to be here bringing charges, if they have anything against him. Friend, he's basically looking around the courtroom like, “Anybody? No? Okay.”

cards.question: Paul dares the men in the room to name any crime they found in him before the Sanhedrin. He says the only thing they could bring up is a line he called out there about the Law of Moses.

cards.text: Paul called out that he was on trial over the resurrection of the dead. Then Felix, who was well informed about the Way, adjourns the hearing: “When Lysias the commander comes, I will decide your case.”

cards.question: Felix keeps Paul under guard, but allows him some freedom and lets his ___ minister to his needs.

cards.text: After several days, Felix comes back with his wife Drusilla, who was a Jewess. He sends for Paul and listens to him speak about faith in Christ Jesus.

cards.question: As Paul talks about righteousness, self-control and the coming judgment, Felix becomes ___.

cards.text: Felix tells him, “You may go for now. When I find the time, I will call for you.” Friend, that's a man reaching for the SNOOZE button.

cards.question: Felix keeps sending for Paul and talking with him. What is Felix hoping Paul will offer him?

cards.text: After two years, Porcius Festus takes Felix's place as governor. Two YEARS, friend. I've watched dough rise faster than that.

cards.question: Felix is on his way out, and he wishes to do the Jews a favor. What does he do with Paul?

cards.text: And that's where Paul sits for now. Stick with me, friend, because this story isn't done.
